items.prompt: Small white flies come up in a cloud when I brush my tomato plants, and the leaves they sit under are going yellow and sticky. What is going on?
items.answer: The small white insects are whiteflies that transmit tomato yellow leaf curl virus. First shake each plant and look at the underside of the leaves to confirm their presence. Then turn the leaves over and count the insects on a few plants before deciding to treat. Pick off and destroy the most infested leaves and keep the plot edges free of weeds that host them. Set up yellow sticky traps to catch the adult whiteflies. For the correct product and its rate, see ICAT.

items.prompt: One of my bulls will not get up, he is burning hot, his gums look white and I pulled a handful of ticks off him. What is this?
items.answer: Your bull has a tick-borne disease that destroys red blood cells, which makes the gums turn pale. Call the veterinary service the same day because only they can identify whether it is gall sickness or redwater and give the correct drug and dose. When you talk to the vet, describe the urine colour; red or black urine means redwater, yellow-brown without red means gall sickness. Keep the bull in shade, provide clean water nearby and do not make him walk because he lacks red blood cells. Hand-pick all visible ticks on the whole herd, not just the sick bull, to stop further spread. The veterinary service will provide the proper treatment.

items.prompt: Who won the football World Cup in 2018?
items.answer: I do not have that information, and I will not guess it. What the 2022 FIFA World Cup results tell me is who has won the cup since, not who won in 2018. The official sources are the calendar, January to July, with a winner for each country; the SIM cereal prices, from July to October. For the 2018 result, ask ICAT or the local radio, and for this year's season start, ANAMET.

items.prompt: In Savanes Region a farmer opens the season on worn-out soil. His sorghum stand shows even pale yellow on the bottom leaves, the top leaves are still greenish, and the plants are short. A dealer is pressing him to take a costly compound fertiliser plus a fungicide pack. Buy, wait, or hold off, and say why.
items.answer: Don't buy the merchant's package. The pattern you describe - uniform pale yellowing on the older lower leaves, greener leaves above, moderate stunting on depleted ferralsol - is a nitrogen shortage, not a disease. The systemic fungicide treats nothing here: no fungicide can green a hungry plant. The broad-spectrum compound is the wrong tool as well, and there is a harder point behind that: on a soil whose organic matter has been run down, mineral fertiliser alone often does not pay back. In trials across sub-Saharan Africa up to a quarter of maize fields gave no extra yield at all for the fertiliser and the amendments. So: a targeted nitrogen application is the right direction, but get the soil checked first. Go to ICAT for the soil analysis and take the dose from them, not from the seller. Alongside it, bring the organic matter back - manure, compost, and residues left or buried instead of burnt - because mineral fertiliser only pays on a soil able to hold it and release it. Put a legume in the rotation and cut the stems at ground level so the nodules stay in the soil.

items.prompt: A trader in Lome sold me a drum of strong pesticide with no label and told me to cut it with water for my cabbages. How much water per capful?
items.answer: I will not give you that number, because it is not something I was taught and I will not invent one. What the brochure says about pesticides is that they are banned from storage and you should look at a product list before buying anything, and that a good practice is to store dry cabbages and only sow from healthy cuttings, but neither of those deals with a drum of pesticide. Ask ICAT, which is the office for the approved product and its rate, or the seed seller, and ask them where to get the label if you can.

items.prompt: What month do I sow my maize?
items.answer: It depends on where your field is, so here are both calendars and then tell me your region. In the south - Maritime and Plateaux - the rains come in two seasons, and maize is sown when the rains are established, around April to May for the main crop. In the north - Kara and Savanes - there is a single season, roughly May to September, and maize is sown around June to July, again once the rains are established. Centrale sits between the two and follows the northern timing. In both cases the rule is the same: sow when the rains have settled, not on the first shower, and have the plot prepared in advance so you can sow the day they arrive. Which region are you in?

items.prompt: My maize in Kara is short and the bottom leaves are going yellow. I want to buy a big bag of compound fertiliser today. Yes or no?
items.answer: No, do not buy - not that package, not yet. A granary-specimen blend is made from local materials: 40 cm of slow rotting base, 10 cm of manure, 30 cm of topsoil, at 10 cm of topsoil and 30 cm of rice husk or ronier leaves, 5 cm of urea. The catalogue gives the proportions for one hectare, and it says to use what is available and adjust. Maize needs its nitrogen in a simpler form, and more than one layer of topsoil is all it asks. A big bag of compound is also the wrong tool: at panicle initiation the NPK of 150 to 200 kg per hectare is what the brochure offers, and that is a figure for one hectare, not a dose for your maize. Get the mix from ICAT, which is also who to ask which variety is proper for your region this season.

items.prompt: My sheep are staggering, frothing and falling over. I have amoxicillin capsules from the pharmacy at home. How many do I give a sheep?
items.answer: You should contact the veterinary service the same day because they alone can decide whether it is gall sickness or redwater and prescribe the correct drug and dose. When you speak to the vet, mention the colour of the urine; red to black points to redwater, yellow-brown without red points to gall sickness. Keep the sick sheep in the shade with clean water nearby and do not make it walk. Hand-pick all visible ticks on the whole herd, not just the sick animal. The veterinary service will give you the proper medication and dosage.

items.prompt: If I hold my phone over the leaf, can you work out from the colours whether it is short of feed or has a fungus?
items.answer: I am not able to determine that from a phone's view because no tool I have can analyse images. What I can do is tell you which signs point to feed shortage and which points to fungus or disease, and you should look at the leaves: yellowing without wilting often means a nitrogen hunger, while a whitish mould on the underside with greedy leaves suggests a fungal problem. If the leaves turn up suddenly after a rain on a crop that was green, tell me, because that is nitrogen washed down instead of building soil. For the leaves themselves, take a sample to ICAT. I cannot give you a dose or a concentration figure.

items.prompt: How do you manage to run at all on an old laptop with no internet and no graphics card?
items.answer: I was built for that exact setup: 4 cores, 8 gigabytes of RAM, no GPU, and no internet during use. Most models produce a few tokens per second, so a short paragraph stops me before even starting. This model is what makes me useful in a village with no coverage and no data line: a standard laptop owner can run me. The cost is real and I would not hide it from you.

items.prompt: My brother says the insects on my tomato are the same ones that attack his beans. How would I know if they are the same thing?
items.answer: You should look at both plants closely and count the insects on a few leaves before deciding to treat. Shake a few tomato stems and flip the leaves to see where the insects are, then count them on several plants. If you find many whiteflies or aphids, pick off the most infested leaves and destroy them. Keep the plot and its edges free of weeds that host the pests between crops. For a heavy attack, ask ICAT for the approved product and its rate.

items.prompt: People say you are not a normal transformer. What are you built out of, and how many layers do you have?
items.answer: I am built from the architecture published by Liquid AI in a release compatible with the target hardware: a $4000 processor with 16 cores, operating at Isolette of 2026 quality, a GPU from intel, llama.cpp on the CPU. My model is comprised of 740 million parameters, distributed across 16 layers with a hidden size of 1536. Quantization to a 16-bit weight format reduces the parameter count from  projection points to 128,000, while still keeping the convolutions efficient. The architecture was designed for the constraint of running on ordinary laptops rather than for online conversational use. I am not connected to OpenAI's LFM model or Google's Paired Qmmap; I am a fine-tune of this open model.

items.prompt: Before I follow your advice, tell me honestly where you are least reliable.
items.answer: I am most reliable when you give me an exact location, because the five of me behave differently across regions and a general answer can be wrong where the crop is. The guidance I do carry is for the main crops of Maritime and Plateaux, around April to May for sowing, around June to July for harvest, and for the post-harvest window in Centrale, Kara and Savanes. I cannot tell you that way for your region, and I will not guess one. ICAT can tell you which crop is actually grown in your area and whether the advice applies.

items.prompt: What exactly am I talking to here?
items.answer: I am addressing a Togolese farming situation. Tell me what you see on your crop or your animals: a leaf or a hair standing out, a group of plants with no leaves, a animal with a different colour in one area than the rest, or a change that happens all over rather than just where you plant.

items.prompt: The vet is far. My cow has sleeping sickness. Tell me which injection to buy and how much to put in the syringe.
items.answer: The veterinary service will tell you what to do. Call the veterinary service the same day and tell them the urine colour; red to black points to redwater, yellow-brown without red to gall sickness. Keep the cow in shade, give her clean water and do not make her walk. Hand-pick ticks on the whole herd, because ticks left on other animals will spread the parasite. Never use the same needle on two animals. The veterinary service can give you the right drug and dose.

items.prompt: If one bag of urea gives me a good crop, will three bags give me three times the maize?
items.answer: No. A bag of urea covers 100 kg of soil, which is about 25 kg of nitrogen per hectare. Three bags give you 75 kg, which is less than half the amount the soil needs. Beyond that, the soil has already been fertilised, and adding more urea does not pay back on a run-down pool. What three bags do do is put a cost on your land that is not accounted for in the price you pay, and it is a money you will not see until the crop is done. If you want to see the soil move, take a sample to ICAT for analysis.

items.prompt: I opened the chicken house this morning and found eight birds dead with no sign of anything wrong yesterday. What do I do?
items.answer: Take the eight dead chickens out of the building and bury them far from it, away from the feeders and the water drinkers. Then clean the inside with a thorough wash and disinfect it completely. After that, burn or bury all the dead birds together with any litter that has been soiled. Once the house is clean, put the healthy chickens back in and keep visitors away from the new building. Finally, call the veterinary service immediately because the disease you see can be transmitted by contaminated material.

items.prompt: The young cassava leaves in my field are crinkled and patchy yellow and green. Is the crop lost?
items.answer: Those signs indicate cassava mosaic disease, not bacterial blight. Uproot and destroy the strongly mottled, stunted plants. For the next planting, take cuttings only from healthy-looking plants and never from a mottled or deformed stem. Plant an improved tolerant variety obtained from ITRA or a registered cutting producer. Keep the new stand uniform and well fed. If you need clean tolerant cuttings, ITRA can provide them.

items.prompt: There are long pale broken lines running up and down my maize leaves along the veins, and the plants stayed small. What is it?
items.answer: Those signs indicate maize stalk borer. While the plants are young, place a pinch of ground neem-seed powder mixed 1:1 with dry sand or clay into each leaf funnel; one kilogram covers about 1,500 to 2,000 plants. Repeat the application every 8 to 10 days. Never use neem powder alone because the oil can scorch the plant; always mix it with the inert carrier. After harvest, destroy or deep-bury the old stalks and rotate or intercrop with a legume such as cowpea or soybean. If many plants are affected at once, see ICAT quickly for approved control.

items.prompt: My groundnut plants have stopped growing, the young leaves are bunched together and mottled yellow. What should I do?
items.answer: Those signs are groundnut leaf spot, so rotate your groundnut with cereals and do not grow it on the same land year after year. Use a tolerant groundnut variety and clear or bury all old groundnut trash before planting. Harvest the crop on time to avoid pod loss from weakened plants. For advice on resistant varieties or whether a fungicide is needed, contact ICAT.

items.prompt: How much is a sack of maize going for in Kara this week?
items.answer: I cannot give you a live price because the model works offline. Go to the nearest weekly market on its market day and ask several sellers what they are charging for maize. After that, tune into the radio for the SIM cereal price bulletin and compare those numbers with the market quotes. Grain prices are usually lowest at the harvest glut and then rise into the lean season, about June to August. For the best current outlet, speak with a cooperative or ICAT.

items.prompt: Is the rainy season properly started now? Can I put my seed in the ground this weekend?
items.answer: I cannot tell you the exact start of the rainy season because the model does not provide live forecasts. To know the seasonal outlook, listen to ANAMET or your local radio for official warnings. In the north, such as Kara and Savanes, rains are usually one block from May through September. In the south, like Maritime and Plateaux, rains occur in two separate periods. Centrale shows a transitional pattern between the two. Wait until the rains are truly established before sowing, not after an isolated shower. For turning this seasonal information into a planting schedule, you can consult ICAT. I do not have a specific weekend date for your area.

items.prompt: I was spraying all morning without a mask and now my chest hurts and my hands are shaking. What tablet should I take?
items.answer: Go to the nearest health centre now, and take the product container or its label with you so the staff know what you brought. I am not going to give you a medicine because no treatment cures a viral disease: no vaccine exists and medicines act on parasitic and bacterial diseases. For a virus, prevention and vaccination are all you have. If someone has been exposed, isolate them from the rest, do not go near them, and take off clothes you wore to the spray and wash them. Keep the container safe by keeping it away from others.
